items.text: The 'Usage Example' in CNA's README.md (section 10) does not compile as written and teaches a double present. It includes Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/GraphicsDeviceManager.hpp, but the header is modules/runtime/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GraphicsDeviceManager.hpp and no forwarding header exists. It calls device.Clear(CornflowerBlue) with only 'using namespace Microsoft::Xna::Framework', but CornflowerBlue is the static member Color::CornflowerBlue and no namespace-scope constant exists. It calls device.Present() at the end of Draw, although GraphicsDeviceManager::EndDraw() already presents every frame whose BeginDraw() succeeded, so each frame is presented twice. Its Update/Draw overrides do not call Game::Update/Game::Draw, which leaves components and FrameworkDispatcher::Update() unpumped. The manuscript's 2026-08-12 session log already calls this the 'stale README double-present pattern' at 7a64362e; README.md was last changed in 9a42a7e82 and still carries it at 009d40f5. This is a documentation defect in CNA's front-page example, not a runtime bug. The site teaches the corrected program (deep-dives/framework/first-game-walkthrough.html).
items.bible_ref: PLAN.md session log, Phase F corrective batch 3

items.text: misc/cnj.md says the failed .cnj existence check that precedes native-extension resolution is 'now serviced by the content-manifest cache ... rather than a raw stat call'. At 009d40f5 ContentManager::ResolveAssetPath still calls std::filesystem::exists for the literal path, the .cnj candidate and each extension candidate. ContentManager.hpp states that the manifest (contentManifest_, built lazily by GetContentManifest/RefreshContentManifest) is 'NOT yet consulted by ResolveAssetPath()/Load<T>()'. The manifest is an introspection snapshot only. This is documentation drift in CNA's CNJ design note (the manuscript's contradiction C-010). The companion claim C-009, a global cnjVersion ceiling of 1, is fixed: cnj.md now documents per-type ceilings.
items.evidence: misc/cnj.md (resolution-order rationale paragraph); modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManager.hpp (contentManifest_ comment; ResolveAssetPath std::filesystem::exists calls)

items.text: docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md section 1 (Ownership Model) says that existing XNA resources hold a std::unique_ptr<IXxxRenderer>, gives ITexture2DRenderer as an example, and says any sharing 'never reaches the public API'. At 009d40f5, Texture2D holds std::shared_ptr<ITextureRenderer> plus shared CPU-pixel and mip vectors, and Texture3D and TextureCube hold std::shared_ptr renderers. Texture2D's copy constructor and copy assignment are defaulted (CNAEXT), so a value copy shares the renderer object. Only VertexBuffer and IndexBuffer (and similar) hold unique_ptr, and the document's section 5 move example uses one of those. This is documentation drift (the manuscript's contradiction C-011). WP08-i011 covers a different sentence of the same document.
items.evidence: docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md (## 1. Ownership Model); modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Texture2D.hpp (renderer_, cpuPixels_, defaulted copy operations); Texture3D.hpp and TextureCube.hpp (renderer_)

items.section: CNA documentation contradictions at the tag
items.text: The EasyGL L7 records disagree with their own machine fields. The goldenComparison.justification of docs/gltf-l7-corpus-report.json and tests/gltf-l7/easygl-policy.json says two independent llvmpipe/EasyGL processes produced byte-identical PNGs 'for all 137 renderable assets', while the same report's fields record distinctAssetCount 148, capturedAssetCount 140 and rejectedAssetCount 8 (docs/gltf-conformance.md also says 140 PNGs plus 8 safe rejections). The manuscript found the same disagreement at the alpha.1 tag, and it survives at 009d40f5. misc/FUTURE.md likewise describes the OPENGLES3 L7 gate as '137 deterministic PNGs plus 8 deterministic safe rejections'. That is 145 dispositions for a 148-asset corpus, but the figure may have been copied from a different campaign, so this part is unclear. This is hand-written prose lagging generated fields, not a rendering defect.
items.evidence: docs/gltf-l7-corpus-report.json (goldenComparison.justification vs capturedAssetCount/rejectedAssetCount); tests/gltf-l7/easygl-policy.json (goldenComparison.justification); docs/gltf-conformance.md (L7 row); misc/FUTURE.md (Phase 5 row)

items.text: The ReadColor/Write(Color) asymmetry that the manuscript recorded is fixed at 009d40f5 (c4561fd2b, 2026-09-04): PacketReader::ReadColor now reads the four bytes that PacketWriter::Write(Color) writes, and PacketReaderTest.ReadColorReadsFourBytesAndInvertsWriteColor asserts the round trip. Three comments still describe the old behaviour. The doc comments of PacketReader::ReadColor in PacketReader.hpp ('Reads a Color value as four 32-bit floats ... Not the inverse of PacketWriter::Write(Color)') and of PacketWriter::Write(Color) in PacketWriter.hpp ('Not the inverse of PacketReader::ReadColor(), which reads four floats') say so, and so does the block comment above WriteColorWritesFourBytes in PacketReaderWriterTests.cpp ('ReadColor() reads 4 floats ... not round-trippable'). The implementation comment in PacketReader.cpp and the second test are correct. This is header and test-comment drift, not a behaviour defect.

items.text: The 'Renderer shader coverage for PBR' table in misc/CNAEXT.md lists EasyGL, Vulkan, SdlGpu, WebGPU ('unskinned', 'no skinning path yet'), D3D11 and D3D9/D3D12, plus a fallback row. At 009d40f5, OPENGL4 builds PBR and skinned-PBR stock programs (OpenGL4StockDraw.cpp: StockProgramShape::Pbr/PbrSkinned), METAL has PBR code, and WebGPU creates and draws skinned-PBR resources (WebGPURenderer.cpp CreateSkinnedPbrResources; DrawFamily::SkinnedPbr). The table therefore understates coverage and keeps a stale WebGPU gap. The manuscript's contradiction C-018 found the same defect in an older form ('derive the table from the tree, never reproduce it'). This is documentation drift; whether each route produces correct PBR pixels is a separate, per-renderer evidence question.
items.evidence: misc/CNAEXT.md (Renderer shader coverage for PBR table); modules/renderers/opengl4/src/OpenGL4StockDraw.cpp; modules/renderers/metal/src; modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp and WebGPURendererModern.cpp
